catalog_locator: p. 5 of the 7-page reprint, paragraph beginning 'El acento prosódico del colorado' rendered at 150 dpi
catalog_quote: El acento prosódico del colorado sigue reglas generales, y algunas palabras se distinguen solamente por el acento. Nótese los ejemplos siguientes: dehuí --- 'escobilla' / déhui --- 'una clase de pescado' / mérana'e --- 'está esperando' / merána'e --- 'está escuchando'. Pero con pocas excepciones, el acento prosódico ocurre en la última sílaba de la raíz de una palabra. Entonces, cuando se agregan sufijos, el acento puede moverse, pasando a uno de los sufijos, o, raramente, a otra sílaba de la raíz. Por ejemplo, en el caso citado de 'merána'e', 'está escuchando', la sílaba "ra" es la última de la raíz; "na" y "'e" son sufijos. Pero nótese como se mueve el acento prosódico al agregar los sufijos "ca" y "'e", haciendo "meracá'e", 'escuchó'. Y en el caso de la palabra "lápalo", 'lagartijo', cuando se agrega el sufijo "chi" resulta "lapalóchi", 'del lagartijo'. La entonación colorada es semejante a la castellana en unos aspectos. Por ejemplo, el tono generalmente es más alto en sílabas con acento prosódico.

new_statements.translation: Colorado stress follows general rules, and some words are distinguished only by stress. Note the following examples: dehuí 'brush', déhui 'a kind of fish', mérana'e 'is waiting', merána'e 'is listening'. But with few exceptions, stress falls on the last syllable of the root of a word. Then, when suffixes are added, the stress may move, passing to one of the suffixes or, rarely, to another syllable of the root. [...] But note how the stress moves when the suffixes 'ca' and ''e' are added, giving meracá'e 'listened'. And in the case of lápalo 'lizard', when the suffix 'chi' is added the result is lapalóchi 'of the lizard'.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Default: primary stress on the final syllable of the root (root-final stress), regardless of following suffixes; but stress is lexically/morphologically contrastive in some pairs (mérana'e vs merána'e, déhui vs dehuí) and certain suffixes (e.g. -ca 'past', -chi) attract or shift stress rightward off the root. Stressed syllables carry higher pitch.
new_statements.exceptions: 'Con pocas excepciones': minimal pairs distinguished only by stress (dehuí/déhui; mérana'e 'is waiting' vs merána'e 'is listening'); stress shifts onto some suffixes (meracá'e) or to another root syllable (lápalo -> lapalóchi). Moore 1966:96 adds that accent 'cambia muchas veces al agregar sufijos' and differs between dialects; Moore 1979 NF12 notes unstressed vowels devoice before the aspiration.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level 'acento prosódico' defined relative to the root; examples are citation forms and inflected verb words; intonation section notes pitch peaks align with the stressed syllable.
new_statements.identity_note: Moore's 1966-1979 SIL work describes 'Colorado' = Tsafiki (colo1256, ISO cof) of Santo Domingo de los Colorados; same language, older exonym. Moore 1966 notes accent differs 'de dialecto en dialecto' and that his accent marks reflect a single (unnamed) dialect in isolation forms.

new_statements.quote: The status of the glottal stop is uncertain. A characteristic feature of Tsafiki is that stress is phonemic, e.g. in meráno ‘to hear’ and mérano ‘to wait’ (Moore 1966: 96).

new_statements.relation_note: Compatible with the catalog record (Moore 1975 [1972]): Moore says stress falls with few exceptions on the last syllable of the root and that 'algunas palabras se distinguen solamente por el acento' with the same pair (mérana'e 'está esperando' / merána'e 'está escuchando'); Adelaar reports only the contrastive half of that statement (his source is Moore 1966: 96, the orthography note of the Llacta dictionary) and is silent on the root-final default. So the per-work label is lexical (unpredictable) (that is all this source asserts) but it does not contradict the catalog's morphological (root-final) reading; it is a secondary one-sentence summary of Moore, adding no placement detail.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Adelaar & Muysken state only that Tsafiki word stress is phonemic (contrastive), illustrated with the minimal pair meráno 'to hear' vs mérano 'to wait', citing Moore 1966: 96; they give no placement rule (no default position, no root-final statement) and say nothing else about stress for Tsafiki anywhere in the book (whole text searched for Tsafiki/Colorado co-occurring with stress/accent/tone/prosod-: only this sentence).
new_statements.exceptions: none; only the one minimal pair
new_statements.identity_note: Tsafiki (Colorado, Tsáchila) of Santo Domingo de los Colorados, western Ecuadorian lowlands; Adelaar's Tsafiki phonology paragraph and consonant table are 'based on Moore 1966' (SIL, Llacta 22 dictionary), i.e. the same variety and the same primary describer as the catalog record.

sources.note: p.5: stress ('acento prosódico') follows general rules and some word pairs are distinguished only by stress (dehuí/déhui, mérana'e/merána'e); with few exceptions stress falls on the LAST SYLLABLE OF THE ROOT; when suffixes are added stress may move onto a suffix or, rarely, to another root syllable (merána'e 'is listening' vs meracá'e 'listened'; lápalo -> lapalóchi). Pitch is generally higher on stressed syllables.
